title: God frees from penalty only while correcting foulness by the Spirit
source_text: VIII. Nec enim quenquam Deus a poena liberum pronunciat, quin simul in eo pravitatem peccati corrigat; & foeditatem tollat, per veram poenitentiam efficaciam ac vim Spiritus Sancti. Neque Christus tantum in hunc finem passus est, ut quod nostra peccata justissime merentur supplicium evaderemus, sed etiam ut nos a peccati corruptione vindicaret, & ex impiis ac peccatoribus justos sanctosque coram Deo redderet.
pass_a_gloss: For God pronounces no one free from penalty unless at the same time he corrects in him the depravity of sin and takes away the foulness, through true repentance and the efficacy and power of the Holy Spirit. Nor did Christ suffer only to this end, that we might escape the punishment our sins most justly deserve, but also that he might vindicate us from the corruption of sin, and from the impious and sinners render us just and holy before God.
pass_b_english: God never frees from penalty without also correcting sin's foulness by repentance and the Spirit.
Christ suffered both to spare due punishment and to make the impious just and holy.
